name: Odd-Torsion Dual Class
definition: Fix $r=3$, put $m=3r+4=13$, and order the vertices $V=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. Start with a two-dimensional simplicial complex $M$ generated by the following three triangles for each $i=0,\ldots,3r-1$: $\{i\bmod3,(i+1)\bmod3,3+i\}$, $\{3+i,3+((i+1)\bmod(3r)),(i+1)\bmod3\}$, and $\{m-1,3+i,3+((i+1)\bmod(3r))\}$. A simplicial complex generated by triangles contains those triangles and all their subsets, but no higher-dimensional faces. Complete its edge set as follows. While an edge is missing, choose the lexicographically least ordered triple $(a,b,w)$ with $a<b$, $w\notin\{a,b\}$, $\{a,b\}$ not an edge, and both $\{a,w\}$ and $\{b,w\}$ edges; add the edge $\{a,b\}$ and triangle $\{a,b,w\}$. The initial graph is connected, and any connected noncomplete graph has a length-two path with nonadjacent endpoints, so the procedure terminates. Let $X$ be the set of three-element subsets of $V$ which are not triangles of the resulting complex. The **Odd-Torsion Dual Class** is the binary class $\mathcal M_3=\{h_v:v\in V\}\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$, where $h_v(T)=1$ if $v\in T$, and $h_v(T)=0$ otherwise. This deterministic construction gives thirteen distinct concepts on 220 coordinates.
comments: The name refers to the Alexander dual of the completed complex, which is the whole-class nonspanning ambiguity complex. The class has Yang dimension ten in characteristic three and nine in every other characteristic. It is a strict finite reverse witness to the characteristic-two example, not an unbounded-ratio separation. The construction and proof are local; no novelty or minimality claim is made.
